html:
Serbian-American inventor and engineer whose alternating current (AC) motor and power system became the basis of the world's electricity grids. Born to a Serbian family in the village of Smiljan, now in Croatia, he studied in Graz and worked in Budapest and Paris before moving to New York in 1884.

He worked briefly for Thomas Edison, who backed direct current, then went his own way. In 1888 he patented his AC induction motor. The industrialist George Westinghouse bought the patents. In the "war of the currents" that followed, AC won because it could carry power over long distances. Westinghouse lit the Chicago World's Fair of 1893 with it and built the great power plant at Niagara Falls in 1895.

Tesla also worked on radio, remote control and the high voltage Tesla coil. His dream of sending power without wires through a giant tower on Long Island failed when money ran out. He died poor in a New York hotel room in 1943. The unit of magnetic field strength, the tesla, is named after him.
